items.summary: Terawatt PV Research forecasts that Inflation Reduction Act-stimulated capital expenditure for U.S. solar manufacturing will reach $12.2 billion by the end of 2026. This cumulative figure represents more than half of all solar PV manufacturing spending since 2001. Annual spending has exceeded $2.5 billion since 2023, with 2024 recording a record $4.14 billion, primarily driven by First Solar and Qcells. The report projects Texas will emerge as the dominant hub for module production in 2026, surpassing Ohio, as the industry expands its domestic capacity.
items.title: IRA drives U.S. solar capex to $12.2B by 2026

key_points: US President Donald Trump is moving from seeking ownership of Greenland to securing a permanent US military security arrangement with Denmark and Greenland.
The trilateral agreement, to be signed in New York, allows the US to establish new military facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, significantly expanding its Arctic presence.
While Denmark asserts the pact respects sovereignty, legal details remain unclear, and the arrangement shifts Arctic security responsibility to NATO rather than solely the US.
items.summary: US President Donald Trump is shifting his strategy regarding Greenland from seeking territorial acquisition to securing a permanent US military security arrangement. He is set to sign a trilateral agreement with Denmark and Greenland at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The pact allows the US to establish military facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, expanding its footprint beyond the existing Pituffik Space Base. While Danish officials assert the agreement respects sovereignty and places security under NATO's collective responsibility, the full legal implications remain unclear. The deal marks a major shift from Trump's earlier demands for ownership, which were firmly rejected by Greenlandic and Danish leaders.
items.title: Trump Shifts Greenland Focus to Military Security Deal

key_points: Anna Tims, a consumer champion for the Guardian, answers reader questions about customer service challenges, including the role of AI and strategies for effective complaints.
She advises remaining calm during interactions, gathering evidence like booking references, and utilizing public platforms like Twitter to escalate issues when necessary.
Tims highlights that while laws like the Consumer Rights Act 2015 exist, enforcement bodies are often overstretched, and she encourages patronizing companies that go the extra mile.
items.summary: Anna Tims, a consumer champion for the Guardian, hosts a live session to address reader inquiries regarding customer service. She notes that while AI tools can assist with troubleshooting, they often fail to resolve specific complaints, leading to repetitive platitudes. Tims advises customers to remain calm, gather all relevant evidence such as booking references, and utilize public platforms like Twitter to pressure companies into action. She highlights that although legal frameworks like the Consumer Rights Act 2015 exist, regulatory bodies are frequently overstretched. Consequently, she suggests patronizing companies that demonstrate exceptional service and checking for proper contact details before committing to a provider.
items.title: Consumer Champion Anna Tims Discusses Customer Service Issues and Tips

key_points: The Income Tax Department added Rs 11.22 crore to a Haryana resident's income due to unexplained cash deposits and loans.
The ITAT Chandigarh tribunal sent the case back to the Assessing Officer to verify if the taxpayer plants 500 trees as a condition.
Failure to meet the tree plantation requirement within one month will result in the restoration of the original income addition order.
items.summary: A Haryana resident faced an income addition of Rs 11.22 crore after the Income Tax Department scrutinized his return for Assessment Year 2017-18, citing unexplained cash deposits of Rs 85.93 lakh and unsecured loans of Rs 9.26 crore. The taxpayer appealed to the ITAT Chandigarh, proposing to plant 500 trees at the Yamuna Bank, Panipat, Samalakha Site as a measure of social responsibility. The tribunal accepted this proposal conditionally, sending the matter back to the Assessing Officer to verify compliance. The taxpayer must complete the plantation or pay for it within one month; otherwise, the original income addition order will be restored. The dispute remains unresolved as the unexplained money has not yet been substantiated.
items.title: Tax Tribunal Grants Conditional Relief for Income Dispute

key_points: Joshua Foster pleaded guilty to causing the death of his two-year-old son who fell from a hotel window in Cyprus.
The father admitted the charge to avoid a long trial and spare his family from reliving the tragedy in court.
items.summary: Joshua Foster, a British man from Essex, pleaded guilty to causing the death of his two-year-old son through a reckless act at the King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort in Chlorakas, Cyprus. The boy fell from the fourth floor on 12 July. Foster admitted the charge to avoid a lengthy trial. His lawyer stated the plea allows the family to move forward without reliving the tragedy in court. A further hearing is scheduled for 5 October.
items.title: British Father Admits Causing Son's Death in Cyprus Hotel Fall

key_points: An armed group closed Valve No. 7 on the pipeline at Libya's Sharara oilfield, causing a pressure buildup and significant production reduction.
The National Oil Corporation warned that continued closure could halt operations and harm the national economy, potentially forcing a force majeure declaration.
items.summary: Libya's largest oilfield, Sharara, has seen crude production slump from an estimated 340,000 barrels per day to about 120,000 bpd after an armed group closed Valve No. 7. The National Oil Corporation stated this closure caused pressure buildup and warned that continued shutdowns would halt exports, harm state revenues, and expose the transport system to risks, potentially necessitating a force majeure declaration.
items.title: Armed Group Blockade Slumps Libya's Sharara Oilfield Production

key_points: Turkish Minister Murat Kurum stated the COP31 Action Agenda aims to raise electricity's share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035.
Kurum emphasized the responsible deployment of artificial intelligence to advance clean technologies and called for global consensus on these goals.
items.summary: Turkish Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change Murat Kurum outlined the COP31 Action Agenda, which targets raising the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. Kurum stressed the need for responsible artificial intelligence deployment to advance clean technologies. The agenda also includes goals to halve municipal waste increases and reduce building energy-use intensity by at least 25%.
items.title: Turkey's COP31 Agenda Targets Global Electrification and AI Governance

key_points: Typhoon Dujuan caused severe flooding and landslides across eastern Japan, resulting in at least four deaths and six missing persons.
The storm triggered widespread disruptions including flight cancellations and power outages for thousands of homes in the Tokyo region.
items.summary: Footage shows flooded streets and rescue efforts following Typhoon Dujuan, which brought torrential rain to the Tokyo region. The storm triggered landslides in Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures, swamped roads, and caused flight cancellations and transport delays. Officials confirmed at least four deaths and six missing persons on Tuesday as search and rescue teams worked in affected neighborhoods. Thousands of homes lost power due to record-breaking rainfall disrupting travel across the capital region.
items.title: Typhoon Dujuan Brings Flooding and Casualties to Japan

key_points: Donald Trump is expected to defend his ongoing war with Iran and boast about US achievements in a UN speech on September 22, 2026.
Analysts note uncertainty about his remarks, while Trump plans to tout his peacemaker role and address skepticism regarding a security deal in Greenland.
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to deliver a speech at the United Nations on September 22, 2026, where he will defend his ongoing war with Iran and highlight his efforts as a peacemaker. The event is overshadowed by concerns over the war's failure to meet White House objectives and economic damage from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Analysts from the International Crisis Group suggest Trump will contrast his peacemaker claims with military operations, while facing skepticism over a security deal in Greenland. Trump also plans to meet with leaders from Britain, Ukraine, Japan, and Venezuela.
items.title: Trump to Defend Iran War and Gaza Efforts at UN

key_points: PureSky Energy has begun commercial operations at McLean 1 Community Solar, its first project in Illinois, dedicated entirely to income-eligible households.
items.summary: PureSky Energy has commenced commercial operations at McLean 1 Community Solar, marking the company's first solar project in Illinois. The 1. 98-MWDC facility in Bloomington-Normal is dedicated exclusively to low- and moderate-income households through the Illinois Solar for All program. Participating subscribers receive guaranteed savings equal to 50% of the value of their solar credits. The project incorporates pollinator-friendly land management practices to enhance biodiversity. Nicholas Topping, VP of community solar at PureSky, stated that dedicating the project to income-eligible households is an important milestone.
items.title: PureSky Energy Launches Illinois Community Solar Project for Low-Income Residents

key_points: The court directed authorities to facilitate deportation or repatriation and address compensation for those detained beyond their sentence completion dates.
items.summary: The Meghalaya High Court ordered the state government to transfer approximately 30 foreign nationals who completed their prison sentences but remained incarcerated to a temporary detention centre in Shillong by September 28. The court, hearing a suo motu matter, directed the transfer to the MBOSE Hostel facility, which has a capacity for around 60 inmates. Authorities were instructed to assist with deportation or repatriation and to address compensation for those detained beyond their sentence completion dates. The matter was posted for further hearing on September 28.
items.title: Meghalaya High Court Orders Transfer of Detained Foreigners

key_points: India condemned Pakistani airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan that killed civilians, reaffirming support for Afghanistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that Pakistan must demonstrate credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes its promises. This demand follows Pakistani airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan's Kunar and Paktika provinces, which India condemned as aggression against a sovereign neighbor. The attacks reportedly killed at least three civilians, a toll confirmed by the United Nations, while Pakistan claimed the strikes killed 28 militants. India reaffirmed its steadfast support for Afghanistan's independence and territorial integrity.
items.title: India demands credible action from Pakistan on cross-border terror before trusting its words

key_points: JSW Group launched Ampstar, a subsidiary manufacturing electric trucks and buses, with a ₹2,500 crore investment in a Maharashtra facility.
Production is scheduled to begin in October 2026, with plans to generate around ₹12,000 crore in turnover at peak utilization.
items.summary: JSW Group has entered the electric commercial vehicle market through its new subsidiary, JSW Greentech Limited, which will operate under the Ampstar brand. The company invested ₹2,500 crore to build a manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, with an annual capacity of 15,000 vehicles. Senior executives stated that production is scheduled to commence in October 2026. At peak utilization, the facility is expected to generate a turnover of around ₹12,000 crore. The group aims to reduce India's dependence on imported fossil fuels by promoting domestic power generation.
items.title: JSW Group enters ECV market with Ampstar brand and ₹2,500 crore investment

key_points: Nordex is launching the N193/7.X turbine with a 7.3 MW capacity and 193m rotor to optimize energy capture at medium- and low-wind sites.
Serial production is scheduled to begin in 2029, with a lower 6.6 MW configuration planned specifically for the German market to meet local grid constraints.
items.summary: Nordex is expanding its Delta4000 onshore wind turbine range with the N193/7.X variant, which combines a 193m rotor with a maximum nominal capacity of 7.3 MW. Designed for medium- and low-wind sites, the turbine uses 95m single-piece blades and retains components from the established platform while allowing flexible power configurations. Nordex states the new model can deliver up to 14% higher energy yield than the N175/6.X at typical low- to medium-wind sites. Serial production is scheduled to begin in 2029, with a specific 6.6 MW configuration planned for Germany to address permitting and grid-connection requirements.
items.title: Nordex Unveils New 7.3 MW Wind Turbine for Low-Wind Sites

key_points: The Eifel District dispatched emergency teams to the scene but declined to comment on further details, while the US Air Force did not immediately respond to inquiries.
items.summary: A military aircraft reportedly crashed near the US Air Base Spangdahlem in Germany on Tuesday. Local authorities in the Eifel region initially stated that one person was injured. The Eifel District dispatched fire and emergency response teams but declined to comment on further details. The US Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the incident.
items.title: Military Aircraft Crashes Near US Air Base in Spangdahlem, Germany
